10 A metal cylinder is suspended vertically in equilibrium by a cord. The diagram shows the cylinder
in four different positions P, Q, R and S.

Which statement explains the variation of the tension T in the cord?
A
At P and at Q, the tension T in the cord is the same because the difference in pressure
between the top and bottom of the cylinder is the same.
B
At Q, the tension T in the cord is less than at P because, at smaller depth, liquid pressure is
smaller.
C
At R, the tension T in the cord is less than at P because atmospheric pressure is less than
water pressure.
D
At S, the tension T in the cord is greater than at P because atmospheric pressure at S exerts
no force on the top or bottom of the cylinder.

hints: Compare how much of the metal cylinder is under water at P, Q, R and S - P and Q are fully submerged while R is partly submerged and S is in air.
Recall that upthrust is the resultant of water pressure on the top and bottom faces, given by pressure difference times area $U = (p_{bottom} - p_{top})A$.
Use vertical equilibrium $T + U = W$ for the cylinder, so any change in submerged volume changes $U$ and therefore changes $T$.
walkthrough: Identify the forces on the cylinder in equilibrium: weight $W$ downwards, upthrust $U$ upwards from the fluid, and cord tension $T$ upwards, so $T + U = W$ and $T = W - U$.
Write upthrust from pressures: if the cylinder has height $h$ and cross-sectional area $A$, then $p_{bottom} - p_{top} = \rho g h$ in water, so $U = (p_{bottom} - p_{top})A = \rho g h A = \rho g V$.

At P and Q the cylinder is fully submerged with the same volume $V$, and the vertical separation $h$ between top and bottom is the same, so $p_{bottom} - p_{top}$ and $U$ are identical despite the different depths.
Therefore $T = W - U$ is the same at P and Q; absolute pressure increases with depth but the difference cancels out.
At R only part of the volume is displaced so $U$ is smaller and $T$ is larger than at P, and at S in air $U$ is negligible so $T$ is approximately $W$, the largest value. This is option A.

A.explanation: Fully submerged at P and Q, the cylinder displaces the same volume of water so upthrust is the same and $T = W - U$ is the same.

B.explanation: Absolute pressure is smaller at Q, but upthrust depends on the pressure difference between top and bottom, not on depth alone.

C.explanation: At R the cylinder is only partly submerged so upthrust is smaller and $T$ is greater than at P, not less.

D.explanation: Atmospheric pressure acts on all surfaces at S and in air upthrust is negligible, so $T$ is greatest at S because there is almost no upthrust.
